correctness.rationale: PASS: With a_i=si+t and gcd(s,t)=1, a_i^k≡t^k mod s. Set h0=r+s−1. Every representation with residue h0 t^k must have number of distinct summands h≡h0 (mod s); h0−s=r−1<r, so at least h0 terms. Positivity and strict growth make M_k=sum_{i=n}^{n+h0−1}a_i^k the smallest such sum, hence M_k−s is bad if positive, yielding N(k)≥M_k−s+1. If M_k−s≤0 the bound is vacuous. Fuller–Nichols Theorem 8 gives N(1)=M_1−s+1 and a_i^k≥a_i; thus endpoint inequality whenever N(k) exists. The argument also works for s=1, t=0 (unit residue ring trivial), and an independent checker validated 9072 parameter tuples; proof is modular, not based on those tests.
